lesson_title: Paper 2 Practice Run: Graphs Are Checklists, Not Artwork
hook_text: The graph question isn't testing your drawing. It's testing five labels. Here they are.
clip_script: Economics Paper 2 is the graph paper — and here's the secret from the marking guideline: a graph is not artwork, it's a CHECKLIST. Five items. One: axes — price, cost and revenue against quantity. Two: curves, each one NAMED — demand, marginal revenue below it, average cost, marginal cost. Three: equilibrium — where marginal cost meets marginal revenue. Four: dotted lines tracing price and quantity to the axes. Five: the shaded rectangle if profit or loss is asked. A shaky curve with all five labels beats a beautiful curve with none — every time. Now watch the marks land on a real one: monopolist, equilibrium at 100 units. Price? Read UP to the demand curve: R150. Cost? R125 off the average cost curve. Profit: 150 minus 125, times 100 — R2 500 economic profit, and it survives the long run because barriers keep rivals out. Same paper, other half: CPI goes 120 to 127,2. Inflation? 7,2 over the OLD 120, times 100 — six percent. Divide by the old index. Always. Five labels, two calculations, one rule. That's the practice run — walk in knowing where every mark lives.
visual_style: A graph assembling as a literal checklist with five tick boxes; labels stamping onto curves; a red-to-green rectangle flashing R2 500; an index dial sweeping 120 to 127,2 and printing 6,0%.
pacing: Counted five-beat build through the checklist, quick confident strikes through the two calculations, clean landing on the one rule.
call_to_action: Do the full practice run and treat every Paper 2 graph as five labels you already know.
